This seems most rationally to be the Place the Apostle refers as to both these Texts.</ns0:note>, I will put my trust in him: And again <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">This is the third Proof, which tho it be literally <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi>'s Words, who complained how him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self and the Children of God in his days were scorned by the World for cleaving to him, yet herein was he a Type of Christ, and in him was it eminently fulfilled: This the word <ns0:hi>Behold</ns0:hi> intimates, it being a matter of great weight and importance to be attended, to be considered and understood by the Church.</ns0:note>, Behold, I, and the children which God hath given me <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">I and my Brethren, Children of the same heavenly Father, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 11.52. and 20.17. 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn.</ns0:hi> 3.1. which my Father of free Grace chose and delivered on my Purchase, and whom he had fitted and wrought by his Spirit, to be brought home by him unto Glory, th<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

By his Incarnation he is of one Nature with all the Hu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man Race, and so is the Head of them: And by his dying for them all the Human Race are made salvable, which Angels are not; and those who repent and believe on him, are actually sanctified and united to him, as his elect and chosen Body, and shall be saved by him.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 15.54, 55.</ns0:note> that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">By his dying on the Cross as <ns0:hi>Testator</ns0:hi> of God's Covenant, and not by his Power as a <ns0:hi>God</ns0:hi> (which was most glorious to himself, but most ignominious to the Devil, according to the Promise, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 3.15.) did he <ns0:hi>abolish,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>bring to nought,</ns0:hi> and render powerless without any Recovery, not by taking away the immortal Life and Being, but the <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, the Strength and Power to kill. For the <ns0:gap reason="foreign">

                     </ns0:gap>, the <ns0:hi>Authority, Right</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Command, the Keys</ns0:hi> of Death are in Christ's Hand only, and he useth the strength of this Execution in it, as to his Enemies; when Sinners become penitent Believers, then his Death satisfying God's Justice for their Sin, hath executed the Power as to Death, which the Devil had by Law against them, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15.56, 57. <ns0:hi>The Sting of Death is Sin,</ns0:hi> that gives him Power; <ns0:hi>and the Strength of Sin is the Law,</ns0:hi> that, unless satisfied for, takes part with Sin; but Christ by dying takes away the Law's Enmity, removes Sin, as to Guilt, Stain and Power, and so brings to nought this Power.</ns0:note>, that is, the devil <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Prince</ns0:hi> himself set here <ns0:hi>collectively</ns0:hi> for all<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> the rest of his evil Spirits, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 25.41. who by his Lies drew Man into Sin, and by Sin stings him to death; having therefore such Power to seduce to sin, he powerfully renders Men ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />noxious to death; and then, as Executioner, having them by the Law delivered into his Hands, putteth forth his Strength to torment and destroy them. Christ by his Death doth with Price and Power redeem them out of his Hand, and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stroys all his Works, takes Possession of them, and brings them through Death to eternal Life.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

They may <ns0:hi>safely trust</ns0:hi> themselves and their Cause with him, and depend on him, he'l never deceive them. He will satisfie God fully, and give him his due, and discharge that Trust reposed on him. And to relying Souls on him, he'l go through his Work, performing all, till they reach that for which they trusted him, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 11.5. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.13. 1 <ns0:hi>Thes.</ns0:hi> 5.23, 24.</ns0:note> high-priest <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">An Officer that was to order Sacrifice, and all matters wherein God was con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerned according to his written Law and Rule. This Priest must be a Man; and a Partnership in our Conditions, both of Temptations and Miseries, must qualifie him for it; of this Office he treats largely in <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 7.8.9 and 10. Amongst the Offi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cers of this kind he is the Prime, Chief, and Head of all that ever God had, and hath in his Person performed and fulfilled what all of them in theirs did but weakly shadow forth. He was actually in the Flesh, installed in it, of which hereafter.</ns0:note>, in things <ns0:hi>pertaining</ns0:hi> to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">The Compass of his Business lieth in all Divine Matters, all those wherein Sinners are concerned with God, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 5.1. Satisfaction, Intercession, And Blessing, are his great Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerns. His principal Work is to bring God and Sinners toge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">

                     </ns0:gap> properly signifieth <ns0:hi>to make out propitious</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>gracious to another by Sacrifice.</ns0:hi> This High Priest by the Sacri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fice of himself, satisfied God's Justice, removed his Wrath, procured his Pardon as to all Sins of Omission or Commissi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on, however aggravated, for Penitent, Believing Sinners, and so makes God and them Friends, and fits them for Commu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nion with Him here, and for the enjoyment of Him for ever, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 5.19, 21.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:548" />18 For in that he himself suffered <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">The Reason foregoing the Spirit illustrates in this Verse, he is such a Merciful and Faithful High-Priest, by being a Sufferer himself, which he could not have been feelingly, but by his being incarnate. So many great, and afflictive Sufferings never any endured but himself; He felt what Sin deserved, and would fasten-on Sinners without his interpo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing, though he were sinless what Terrors from God with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in, what Pains in his Body without did he suffer and un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dergo; such as are unparallell'd, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 12.3.</ns0:note> being tempted <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">Not from any Corruption or Sin within him, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 14.30. <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 4.15. but from an inveterate Enemy; the Devil without him, and all the Instruments he used of his Associated Spirits and Men: How early on the entrance on his Office did the De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vil begin with him, and thought to have foiled him as he did the first <ns0:hi>Adam</ns0:hi>? and how did his Children tempt him, with the which the Gospel is filled in so many Pages? by these he felt what Temptations were, how difficult to avoid Sin under them, how fearful: it was to be exercised by them, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 5.7. how much such as miscarry under them are to be pitied, what sore Evils Sin brings on the commit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters of it; what succour, strength, stablishing, settlement his Brethren need under it, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 22.43, 44. and how easily with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out his assistance his Tempted Ones may be foiled by it.</ns0:note>, he is able to succour them that are tempted <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Now sensibly made sit by his own Sorrows, Temptations and Sufferings, he is powerfully inclined to help his; sub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />jected he was to all of them, to make him feelingly, tenderly pittying of us. He had the Mercies of God be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore, and as if that were not enough, the Tempted Nature of a Man, to soften his Heart to pity his Brethren in their Sufferings and Temptations. These Sufferings of his had a purchasing Power and Ability in them for us, He there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />by buying help and succour for us as to all ours, that should be correspondent into his; so as by his Bloody Death under Temptation he bought off ours, either not to overtake us, or if under them, he is habitually and meri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />toriously thereby to succour his, most compassionate<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly and readily giving forth all reasonable, suitable, and suf<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ficient support under, and remedy against all these Temp<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tations, which for Sin, or from it, his Brethren are afflicted with, and come to him for help. This is the most pow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />erful Preservative against Despair, and the firmest ground of Hope and Comfort, that ever Believing, Penitent Sinners could desire or have; from all which these <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> might have been convinced what little reason they had to be of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fended with his Humiliation or Death, who was their <ns0:hi>Mes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />siah</ns0:hi>; and though for State and Time a little lower than the Angels, yet in the Humane Nature was thereby exalted to be the Lord and Head above them all.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
